entry.author: Climate Change Commission
entry.summary:
The Climate Change Commission is calling for evidence on the next National Climate Change Risk Assessment (NCCRA), which identifies and assesses Aotearoa New Zealand's most significant climate risks and how to manage them.

In this webinar aimed at people working with communities, local government and NGOs, we shared information about the kind of evidence we’re looking for, the risks we have identified, and how you can get involved.
 
This call for evidence closes on 31 March 2025. Read more about the NCCRA and share evidence online: https://haveyoursay.climatecommission.govt.nz/comms-and-engagement/call-for-evidence-nccra2026/

Want to hear about future events?
• Follow us on Eventbrite: https://www.eventbrite.co.nz/o/climate-change-commission-29793944859
• Sign up to our events mailing list: https://confirmsubscription.com/h/t/2DB84EBFF23E1BC9

12:56 Building our list of risks
17:40 Next steps and how you can be involved

Q&A

23:19 How we've defined and approached risks
24:13 The warming modelling scenarios we will be using
26:10 Timeline for risk identification and releasing our risk list
27:15 Spatial scale for our assessment
28:38 How we can avoid doubling up with evidence collection
30:38 What outcomes and actions came from the first NCCRA
33:11 Whether urban planners will be represented in the reference group
33:36 What the definition of transport includes in this work
34:15 Central government vs local government's roles
35:08 Does adaptation action clash with NZ's emissions reduction plan?
36:40 Risk and consequences of those risks

40:20 High emissions scenarios to stress test risks
41:20 Tapping into existing technical expert groups

49:19 Novel vs traditional attribution techniques
50:13 New domains and reference scenarios since the last NCCRA
